item.title: Ecosystem Components
item.description:
Related repositories and samples:

  • Main runtime: apache/dubbo-go
  • Samples: apache/dubbo-go-samples
  • Generic invocation sample: dubbo-go-samples/generic
  • Nacos registry sample: dubbo-go-samples/registry/nacos
  • Triple sample: dubbo-go-samples/rpc/triple

This page gives a current map of the main Dubbo Go ecosystem repositories. Some older documents still refer to repositories or tools under dubbogo/*; for daily development, use the Apache repositories below as the primary entry points.

dubbo-go

github.com/apache/dubbo-go

The main Dubbo Go runtime repository. It includes:

  • core runtime code
  • built-in protocols, registries, filters, routers, and load balancers
  • tools such as tools/protoc-gen-go-triple
  • tools such as tools/dubbogo-cli

dubbo-go-samples

github.com/apache/dubbo-go-samples

item.title: Generic Invocation
item.description:
Related samples:

  • Generic invocation sample: dubbo-go-samples/generic
  • Triple sample: dubbo-go-samples/rpc/triple

See also: Source Code Guide: Generic Call.

Generic invocation lets a caller invoke a remote service without generated stubs for the target interface. It is commonly used in gateway, testing, interoperability, and dynamic invocation scenarios.

Recommended Entry

For current Dubbo Go, the recommended entry is:

  • client.NewGenericService(...)
  • filter/generic.GenericService.Invoke(...)
  • filter/generic.GenericService.InvokeWithType(...)

This is the normal runtime path for new generic invocation code. Older config.ReferenceConfig-style examples are compatibility paths and should not be the default choice for new docs.

item.title: Using Nacos as a Registry
item.description:
Related samples:

  • Nacos registry sample: dubbo-go-samples/registry/nacos
  • Application-level discovery reference: dubbo-go-samples/registry/nacos

See also:

  • Application-level Service Discovery
  • Tools: dubbogo-cli

This page is a current reference for using Nacos as a registry with Dubbo Go. Older versions of this page described a CLI debugging flow; that content is no longer the main Nacos integration path.

What the Nacos Sample Demonstrates

The current registry/nacos sample shows:

  • provider registration into Nacos
  • consumer lookup through Nacos
  • Triple-based RPC call flow
  • registry-backed service discovery for Go applications
